reference.title: Question Details
reference.shortdesc: A table of survey question details

refbody.example: Qualtrics easily handles most common survey question types including:

property.propvalue: Description from the Qualitrics Website of What the Question Type Commonly is Used For
Multiple choice questions form the basis of most research. They can be displayed as a traditional list of choices or as a dropdown menu, select box, etc.
Text entry is used to gather open-ended feedback from respondents. These responses can be lengthy essays or short text.
Matrix table is used to collect multiple pieces of information in one question. This type provides an effective way to condense your survey or to group similar items into one question.
Sliders let respondents indicate their level of preference with a draggable bar rather than a traditional button or checkbox.
Gather standard form information such as name and email address.
Rank order is used to determine each respondent’s order of preference for a list of items.
Side by side questions let you ask multiple questions in one condensed table and provides an effective way of shortening your survey while gathering the same amount of data.
NPS® tracks customer loyalty with one simple, standardized question: “On a scale from 0-10, how likely are you to recommend our company to a friend or colleague?”
This hidden question is used to time—as well as limit—how long participants spend on a page of the survey.
This variation of the slider question has respondents use various graphic options, such as changing a frown to a smile or choosing a grade, to indicate their level of preference.
Pick, group, and rank is used for sorting activities. Respondents place items into groups and have the option to rank the items within the group.

refbody.example: The basic instructions for setting up a survey do not differ markedly by question type.
